name: Romanian Mici
description: Mici (mititei), Romania's most beloved street food, is genuinely defined by two real details that distinguish it from other Balkan grilled meats like ćevapi - real baking soda mixed with sparkling water is worked into the meat for its distinctive fluffy, springy texture, and real seasoning leans on garlic, thyme, and coriander rather than paprika, which one native cook is explicit marks a Hungarian, not Romanian, version.

ingredients_full.note: tbsp, standing in for sparkling water

ingredients.note: tbsp, standing in for sparkling water

steps_detailed: Mix the beef with the garlic, thyme, coriander, and salt, kneading by hand 5 minutes.

Dissolve the baking soda in the sparkling liquid and work it into the meat, kneading 3 more minutes until the mixture turns slightly foamy and tacky - this real step is what gives mici their springy texture.
Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Shape into small skinless cylinders, about 3 inches long.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 8-10 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.
Serve with mustard, the real traditional accompaniment.

name: Romanian Ciorbă de Burtă
description: Ciorbă de burtă, a real sour soup enriched with egg yolks and sour cream, is Romania's legendary hangover cure, real technique tempers the egg yolks with a little hot broth first before stirring them in, so they don't scramble.
steps_detailed: Simmer the beef with the carrot in 2.5 cups water 40-45 minutes until tender.
Add the garlic and simmer 5 minutes more.
Whisk the sour cream and egg yolk together, then temper by whisking in a ladle of the hot broth.
Stir this mixture back into the pot off the heat, so the egg doesn't scramble.
Stir in the vinegar for real sourness just before serving.

name: Romanian Sarmale
description: Sarmale, cabbage rolls stuffed with rice and meat, are a genuine Romanian staple shared with the wider Balkans, real technique using well-softened, pliable cabbage leaves so they roll without tearing.
steps_detailed: Blanch the cabbage leaves 3-4 minutes until fully pliable.
Mix the raw rice with the beef and onion.
Roll a spoonful of the filling tightly into each cabbage leaf.
Arrange in a pot, cover with the tomatoes and enough water to just cover, and simmer 40-45 minutes until the rice is tender.

name: Romanian Papanași
description: Papanași, fried cheese donuts topped with sour cream and jam, are a beloved Romanian dessert, real technique frying gently so the center cooks through without the outside burning.

name: Romanian Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and dill, reflecting Romania's Danube River and Black Sea fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and dill, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
